A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Scalable Option Learning (SOL). Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and corresponding content can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original throughput measurements and agent-training results on MiniHack, NetHack and PointMaze, including additional PointMaze results in Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results, throughput measurements, learned-reward experiments and extensive behavioral analyses and ablations in Appendix E.

M1.justification: v3 introduces SOL+DIAYN: an online discriminator learns to identify options, and its probabilities supply rewards for non-task options (Section 5.3 and Appendix B.3). This adds a substantive reward-learning component previously left as future work. SOL's shared network, option-switch bootstrapping and adaptive durations already existed in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ZombieHorde and TreasureDash, NetHack with Monk, Ranger and Archaeologist, and PointMaze U-Maze, G-Maze, Medium and Large layouts. The additional-character results move to v3 Appendix E.1; they are not new coverage. Learned-reward experiments and ablations use retained environments.

E2.justification: v3 adds Hierarchical RLLib to the NLE throughput comparison (Table 1) and compares learned-reward SOL against handcoded SOL and APPO in Figure 5. Existing baselines remain. MOC gains a PointMaze curve, but its evaluation and outcomes were already reported in v1 Table 6.

E3.justification: Reported NetHack training increases from 20 billion steps in v1 Section 5.2 to 30 billion in v3 Section 5.1. Common MiniHack/NetHack settings change from batch size 57372 to 32768 and reward scaling 0.1 to 0.01; controller settings and sweep ranges also change. New analyses introduce evaluation-episode protocols and duration, option-quality and PPO-epoch controls. These reported revisions do not establish which retained curves were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's option-behavior analysis, v3 adds controlled tests of bootstrapping, fixed versus adaptive durations, duration-set size, reward scaling, redundant or useless options, and PPO update epochs (Appendices E.3–E.7). Appendix E.2 adds policy-overlap measurements and controller behavior conditioned on health and experience, substantially expanding mechanism and sensitivity analysis.

E5.justification: NetHack reporting changes from three seeds with one-standard-error shading in v1 Figure 4 to five seeds with two-standard-error shading in v3 Figures 3 and 9. v3 also reports uncertainty over 500 evaluation episodes for option returns. The main MiniHack and PointMaze comparisons retain two-standard-error shading over ten seeds.

E6.justification: v3 provides extended NetHack results under revised settings and new SOL+DIAYN results showing slower learning but similar final MiniHack performance to handcoded SOL. New ablations report component-removal degradation and task-dependent effects of additional PPO epochs. Table 10 adds policy-overlap values of 0.154, 0.018 and 0.388. Reported SOL throughput changes from approximately 42000 to 43000 steps/second; these are updated reports, not an established same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 corrects the bootstrap state's index from t+K in v1 to t+K+1 in v3, matching the displayed reward sum through K. The principal value and advantage definitions remain in the corresponding algorithm appendices. The new mechanism discussion does not introduce a theorem or formal proof framework.

C1.justification: The central claim that scalable hierarchical learning outperforms flat agents remains. v3 narrows the billion-sample novelty claim to online hierarchical RL, changes the abstract's throughput claim from 25x to approximately 35x and its training scale from 20 to 30 billion frames, and foregrounds algorithmic contributions alongside systems engineering.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations concerning option degeneracy, non-stationarity, state-dependent coordination, duration selection and sample-efficiency tradeoffs. Appendix A replaces the assumption of entirely supplied rewards with a qualified discussion of learned rewards and their limited generality. It also removes v1's substantive limitation that options cannot be interrupted mid-execution, although the described duration mechanism still selects lengths beforehand.

D1.justification: v3 supplies discriminator architecture, training loss, optimizer details and hyperparameter sweeps for SOL+DIAYN. It also adds network parameter counts, the discount factor, Cython implementation information, an overall training listing and expanded wrapper/trajectory documentation. Reported NetHack runtime is revised. These additions substantially improve implementation documentation; the existing code-release location and hardware platform remain.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds focused comparisons with Agent57 and Park et al.'s offline hierarchical scaling work. It revises the relationship to hierarchical PPO methods from special cases of SOL's objective to distinctions involving bootstrapping and duration selection. New references support the degeneracy and non-stationarity discussion, while the broader research positioning remains hierarchical RL at scale.

P1.justification: v3 substantially rewrites and reorganizes the method exposition, consolidates the MiniHack and NetHack experimental sections, relocates detailed definitions and multi-character discussion to appendices, and restructures limitations and impact material. These changes extend beyond the prose needed to introduce new experiments.

P2.justification: The main paper changes to a two-column layout. The throughput bar chart becomes a table; NetHack plots are reorganized into separate LLM and non-LLM comparisons; the G-Maze illustration moves to the appendix. v3 adds an architecture diagram and numerous diagnostic plots, and replaces the original behavior display with expanded bar charts and distributions.

improvement.justification: v1 leaves reward discovery entirely to future work and provides little controlled evidence about SOL's individual components. v3's learned-reward experiment and extensive ablations directly address these important gaps, while expanded implementation details and five-seed NetHack reporting strengthen reproducibility and empirical support. Automatic reward learning is demonstrated only on the two MiniHack tasks, and removing the interruption limitation weakens transparency, but these qualifications do not outweigh the substantial gains.
